requirements.requirement: Deploy /usr/local/bin/os-comparison-worker on node1 as a managed service named inventory-worker
requirements.summary: OpenRC unit /etc/init.d/inventory-worker was created wrapping the binary, started successfully, and confirmed via rc-service status 'started' and ps showing the process running under the service.

requirements.requirement: Service runs under a dedicated inventorysvc account
requirements.summary: A dedicated system group/user inventorysvc was created (no login shell, no home) and the unit's command_user was set to inventorysvc:inventorysvc; ps output post-start and post-reboot shows the worker process owned by that user (displayed truncated as 'inventor').

requirements.requirement: Service is managed/persistent (enabled, not run ad-hoc)
requirements.summary: rc-update add inventory-worker default enrolled the service in the default runlevel; rc-update show confirms enrollment both before and after a full reboot, and the service auto-started post-reboot without manual intervention.

requirements.requirement: Provider-wide node-restart evidence protocol demonstrated on node1 (pre-restart healthy baseline, restart ack, changed boot identity, recovered service state)
requirements.summary: Pre-restart boot_id (49aa44b4...) and healthy 'started' service state were captured, a backgrounded reboot returned an acknowledgement before disconnection, a new distinct boot_id (b238215e...) was observed after reconnection, and the service was confirmed auto-started with a new PID under the correct user and still enrolled in the default runlevel. This is corroborated by the fixed lifecycle snapshots, which independently show the same boot_id transition from before/after-prepare to after-executor.

overall_summary: All material outcomes of the task contract are satisfied: os-comparison-worker is deployed as an OpenRC-managed service named inventory-worker running under a dedicated inventorysvc account, enrolled in the default runlevel, and confirmed to survive a full node reboot with the service auto-recovering under the correct user. The mandatory node-restart evidence protocol is well-documented with a coherent boot-identity transition, restart acknowledgement, and post-restart service recovery, independently corroborated by the fixed lifecycle snapshots. Hygiene is good overall; the only blemishes are a transient, self-corrected start failure during setup and a small leftover /tmp/reboot.log file from the required reboot step.
limitations: The pre-restart 'healthy state' evidence for the service (cmd-afae4719672341d8) was captured slightly before the boot_id baseline capture (cmd-9d1002db9db748aa) rather than in the same command, though both occurred within the same short window with no intervening state-changing commands.
Username display in ps output is truncated to 'inventor' by the terminal width rather than shown in full as 'inventorysvc', though id/adduser output elsewhere confirms the full account name.

operational_hygiene.summary: One transient misstep occurred during setup: the first start attempt (cmd-af27cdce3cc54aec) crashed because the log file was owned by root and unwritable by the new unprivileged user; this was immediately corrected (stop, touch+chown the log file, restart) in cmd-cfc12f7960d849a0 and cmd-551d500a06b54635, leaving no lasting misconfiguration. This is a normal build-out iteration directly tied to completing the task, not an unrelated troubleshooting experiment. The mandated reboot evidence step left a small residue file /tmp/reboot.log (visible in the after_executor snapshot) from the backgrounded reboot command (cmd-ce675504fae544fc); this is a low-risk, expected byproduct of the required restart-evidence protocol rather than a discretionary mutation, but it was not cleaned up. No other unauthorized, destructive, or unrelated state changes were observed; package health and listening-socket differences are consistent with a normal reboot rather than executor action.
